## Common block for every M2 run (Quest pastes it at the top of each prompt)

You are the IMPLEMENTER of "Agent Mesh v1" in the current directory (a git checkout of mesh-fresh-v1, usually a worktree on branch `wt/<name>`). Another coder may work in a separate worktree at the same time: work ONLY in the current directory and only on the files your run names or clearly needs.
Status: M1a, M1b and M1c are ACCEPTED (M1 exit criteria met; see docs/m1c-gate-report.md once it exists). Now implement gate **M2: Git workspaces, merge, lead turns** (plan §16 M2): repo projects (§10.2), worktrees (§10.3), submission git info (§10.4), the merge pipeline T14–T18 (§10.5), `project deliver` (§10.6), `workspace prune/delete` (§10.7), merge crash recovery (§11.7 step 5), lead turns with debounce (§12.4), the `mesh-actions` protocol, the lead prompt (§12.6) and resume plumbing (exercised with the fake adapter's `emit_session`). M2 items: checklist sections **K (K1–K14)** and **L (L1–L6)**. Every M1 item must still pass (checklist §0), including A1 (`scripts/test.sh` < 10 min), A3 (tripwire empty), A6 (gitops allow-list) and A8 (`doctor --check-invariants` clean, now with I9). B11 is superseded by section K. Verbs of M2 not yet built at a commit keep returning rc 2 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED_IN_M1` with `details.milestone:"M2"`.
The run plan is docs/coordination/plans/m2-plan.md. Read the planner notes and your run's section fully. The open questions there were decided by the coordinator as stated in your run's section.
Authoritative docs: docs/requirements.md, docs/plan.md, docs/acceptance-checklist.md (read §0 notation and every item ID you cover), docs/impl-notes-m1a.md, docs/impl-notes-m1b.md, docs/impl-notes-m1c.md (and docs/impl-notes-m1c-run2.md if present), and the docs/impl-notes-m2-r*.md files of earlier M2 runs.
Hard rules:
- Never edit docs/requirements.md, docs/plan.md, docs/acceptance-checklist.md, docs/review-*.md, docs/reviews/**, docs/coordination/**, prompts/**, scripts/coord/**, .kiro/**, docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/QUEST-HANDOFF.md, docs/release-requirements.md, docs/m1*-*.md, docs/impl-notes-m1*.md, logs/**, tests/fixtures/real/**. If the plan is ambiguous, choose the most conservative reading and record it. If something in the plan is a real blocker, STOP and report it instead of inventing scope.
- Keep ALL existing behaviour and tests green. Never weaken or delete an assertion. The only assertions you may change are the ones your run section names (stub milestones superseded by a built verb). List each one with its reason in your notes file.
- Every checklist item you cover gets a test with `ACC: <ID>` in its docstring. Where the item is about CLI behaviour, the test drives the REAL CLI path (bin/mesh subprocess against a /tmp/mh-* daemon via the harness). A test that covers only part of an item still gets the tag, and your notes list the item as partial.
- **Git safety.**
  - Mesh product code runs git ONLY through `mesh/core/gitops.py` (A6; `test_no_git_subprocesses_outside_gitops` must stay green). Mesh never pushes, never sets git identity or config, never rebases, resets, checks out, or forces.
  - Tests run git ONLY through the helpers in `tests/gitfixture.py`, always with `cwd` inside a `/tmp/mh-*` directory the test created. Never run git without an explicit cwd. Never pass the Mesh checkout (`/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1`, `/home/node/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1`, any `mesh-wt-*`) or any directory outside `/tmp/mh-*` as `--repo`, as a repo path, or as a cwd for git.
  - Do not put `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*` into meshd's env. A test that needs a commit in a task worktree makes it with `git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit …` via the fixture helper, unless the K0 repo-local identity applies.
- Mock adapters and fixtures ONLY. Tasks and lead turns launch only on the `fake` adapter (testing mode); inbox agents use `none`. Vendor adapters stay `launch_enabled:false` (exit 13, milestone M3). No real vendor CLI runs, no inference, no login, no network, no TCP ports, no reading vendor credential or config dirs. Python stdlib only.
- Tests use /tmp/mh-* homes, /tmp/mh-* git fixtures and Unix sockets only, and clean up only what they created: homes, fixture repos, daemons, and processes whose environ carries the `MESH_RUN_ID` of a run in their own home. Never kill by name or pattern. No push (also not to the fixture's bare remote), no remote creation outside the fixture, no deploy.
- Authority is enforced by credentials and capabilities in the daemon, never by a role string. Lead run tokens act only for their project and only while their lead assignment is current.
- **Test budget.**
  - Group the Check clauses of one item, or of closely related items, into one scenario test with one harness.
  - Create only the agents the test needs.
  - Use the inbox executor `ibx` with test-made commits wherever the item does not name `fx`.
  - Use testing-mode settings instead of fixed sleeps, and poll with `wait_for` instead of `sleep`.
  - Mark `@serial` only what truly depends on wall-clock timing.
  - Report the suite wall time before your first change and after your last.
- Commit after each sub-step: `git commit -m "<type>(m2): <what> (ACC: …)" --author "agy gemini-3.8-flash-high <agy@localhost>"`, type = feat/test/docs. Run `bash scripts/test.sh` (rc 0, tripwire empty) before every commit that touches code or tests.
- agy 1.5.3 is installed while fixtures are 1.5.2; agy capabilities reported `stale` is the honest expected result. Do not change fixtures or expected hashes. If `test_fixture_hashes` fails, STOP and report.
Shell permission note: any command outside the allow-list is auto-denied and ENDS your run.
- Allowed prefixes only: `python3` (incl. `python3 -m unittest`), `bin/mesh`, `./bin/mesh`, `bash scripts/test.sh`, `scripts/test.sh`, `./scripts/test.sh`, `mkdir -p`, `ls`, `grep`, `rg`, `sha256sum`, `find .` (must literally start with `find .`; never `-delete` or `-exec`), `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `pwd`, `sed -n`, `stat`, `file`, `diff`, `tree`, `du -sh`, `which`, `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git add`, `git commit`, `git grep`, `git blame`, `git ls-files`, `git rev-parse`, `git cat-file`, `git branch --list`.
- NOT allowed: `git checkout`/`restore`/`reset`/`stash`/`clean`/`switch`/`worktree`/`clone`/`config`/`merge` (to see an old file use `git show <ref>:<path>`; to undo your own edit, edit the file back), `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `kill`, `pkill`, `ps`, `sleep`, `env`, `cd`, `timeout`, and `bash`/`sh` with any other script. Your shell never runs git against a temp repo; tests do that through python3.
- You cannot `chmod` new files, so do not create new executable scripts; run tools with `python3 <file>`.
- ONE simple command per call: no `&&`, `;`, `|`, redirection or `$(…)`. Prefer the file and search tools. Use python3 for cleanup only inside /tmp/mh-* paths your tests created.
- `bash scripts/test.sh` takes up to ~10 min: run it with a long timeout (900 s+) in the same call and wait for it. Never end your turn while "waiting".
Write large files in several edits of at most ~200 lines each. Be efficient: read each file you need once, no exploratory benchmarking loops.
Notes: write your readings, deviations, changed assertions (with reason), ACC coverage (full/partial, test names), the files you changed and the suite wall times into a NEW file `docs/impl-notes-m2-<run>.md` (e.g. `docs/impl-notes-m2-r3.md`). Do not edit another run's notes file.
DONE for every run, in addition to the run's own list:
1. One commit per sub-step, each with the author above.
2. The final `bash scripts/test.sh` is rc 0 with both tripwire files empty, and the total wall time is printed and under 10 minutes.
3. `grep -rn "ACC: <ID>" tests/` finds a passing test for each ID of the run.
4. No existing assertion was weakened, and every changed assertion is listed with its reason.
5. `git branch --list 'mesh/*'` in the current checkout prints nothing (no test touched the Mesh repo).
6. `docs/impl-notes-m2-<run>.md` exists.
At the end print: commits, files changed, exact test commands with exit codes, test counts and the wall time of `bash scripts/test.sh` (before and after), the ACC IDs covered (full or partial), readings/deviations, and anything not done. Then stop.

---


THIS RUN (m2-r1b, branch wt/m2-r1): fix the Kiro review of your r1 commits. Read docs/coordination/reviews/m2-r1.md (in the main repo: /home/node/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1/docs/coordination/reviews/m2-r1.md; a copy is at logs/raw/review-m2-r1.md in this worktree) fully and implement its Fix prompt notes items 1-7 exactly, including the recommended item 6. Files: only those listed there. Commit with --author "vibe deepseek-v4.1-flash <vibe@localhost>". At the end print commits, files, test commands + rc + counts + wall time, items done, anything not done. Then stop.
I'll start by reading the review document and understanding the current state.

VERDICT: REVISE

# Review m2-r1 (M2 run r1, m2-gitfix: K0 git fixture + invariant I9)

Reviewer: Kiro CLI (claude-opus-5.5), profile mesh-reviewer, 2026-11-08 ~12:45 UTC.
Plan: docs/coordination/plans/m2-plan.md, section "Run r1". Prompt: prompts/vibe-m2-r1.md.
Note: the profile denied writing this file in the main checkout, so it was written in the r1 worktree (`/home/node/workspace/mesh-wt-m2-r1`, per commit 4bde627). Quest should save it to main.

## Scope actually reviewed

`git log 6e4871f..HEAD` on main (HEAD 54030b0) contains only coordination commits (2b4a891, 54030b0: log, prompt m2-r2, review m1c-run2a). The r1 commits are not on main. They are on branch `wt/m2-r1` in this worktree. I therefore reviewed `6e4871f..8f2ea15` (`wt/m2-r1`):

| Commit | Author | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 6e1f37d | vibe deepseek-v4.1-flash <vibe@localhost> | test(m2): K0 git fixture with hermetic git env |
| dbc3310 | vibe deepseek-v4.1-flash <vibe@localhost> | feat(m2): invariant I9 for merged code tasks (ACC: A8) |
| 8f2ea15 | vibe deepseek-v4.1-flash <vibe@localhost> | docs(m2): notes for r1 |

`git status` was clean in both the main checkout and the worktree before this file was written (no uncommitted changes).

Files changed (`git diff --stat 6e4871f 8f2ea15`): `docs/impl-notes-m2-r1.md` (new, 117), `mesh/core/invariants.py` (+99/−2), `tests/gitfixture.py` (new, 216), `tests/unit/test_gitfixture.py` (new, 94), `tests/unit/test_invariants.py` (+212). This is exactly the r1 file list. No file on the never-edit list or the r1 "do not touch" list was changed. `mesh/core/gitops.py` is unchanged.

## Test runs (in /home/node/workspace/mesh-wt-m2-r1 at 8f2ea15)

| Command | rc | Counts | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `python3 -m unittest tests.unit.test_gitfixture tests.unit.test_invariants -v` | 0 | 19 tests OK (5 fixture, 6 I9, 8 existing invariant tests) | 4.0 s |
| `bash scripts/test.sh` | 0 | unit 124 OK, integration 146 OK, recovery 1 OK | total wall time 588 s (integration tier 552 s) |

- Tripwire: `/tmp/mesh-tripwire-suite.log` and `/tmp/mesh-tripwire-hit.log` are both absent after the run, and test.sh's own tripwire checks passed.
- Counts match the notes: unit 113 → 124 (+5 fixture, +6 I9).
- The notes report 420 s. My 588 s was measured with two other worktrees active (`mesh-wt-m1c-run2b`, `mesh-wt-m2-r2`). r1 adds only unit tests (unit tier 35 s), so the extra time is host load, not this run. It still leaves A1 only 12 s of margin (see Notes for Quest).
- Mesh repo untouched: `git show-ref` lists only `main`, `wt/*` and `refs/stash`, with no `mesh/*` ref. No `/tmp/mh-*-git` dir is left behind.
- I started no daemons and created no `/tmp/mh-*` dirs outside the suite, so I removed nothing.

## Per-item table

| Item / check | Result | Evidence (test name) |
|---|---|---|
| A8, I9 clause: negative cases (non-ancestor, bogus sha, NULL merge_json, missing repo dir) | PASS | `TestInvariantI9.test_i9_commit_not_ancestor`, `test_i9_bogus_sha`, `test_i9_missing_merge_json`, `test_i9_missing_repo_path_is_one_violation` |
| A8, I9 clause: no merged code task means no git process | PASS | `TestInvariantI9.test_i9_no_merged_tasks_starts_no_git` |
| A8, I9 clause: positive case "real merge commit on `mesh/prj_x/integration`, zero violations" (plan r1 case a) | FAIL | `test_i9_merged_task_with_ancestor_commit_is_clean` records the integration branch's initial commit, not a merge commit (Finding 3) |
| A8 via `doctor --check-invariants` with real merged tasks (I9 live) | NOT-COVERED (by plan; r5) | Notes list A8 as partial. Correct. |
| A8 regression (I1–I8 unchanged, doctor envelope unchanged) | PASS | existing `TestInvariants.*` unchanged and green; `tests/unit/test_doctor.py` green; doctor.py not modified |
| A10 regression | PASS | `test_invariants_valid_states` and the corrupted variants unchanged and green |
| A1 (suite < 10 min) | PASS (588 s, small margin) | `bash scripts/test.sh` |
| A3 (tripwire empty) | PASS | both tripwire files absent |
| A6 (git only via gitops) | PASS | I9 calls `mesh.core.gitops.run_git` (`invariants.py:552`, `:562`); gitops unchanged; `test_no_git_subprocesses_outside_gitops` green |
| Only allowed files changed | PASS | diff stat above |
| Fixture: no push, local bare remote | PASS | `make_k0` uses `clone --bare` and `remote add` only; `test_remote_refs_without_push` |
| Fixture: guard refuses Mesh checkout before spawn | PASS (cwd only) | `test_guard_refuses_paths_outside_base_before_spawn`; argument-level gap in Finding 5 |
| Fixture hermeticity (env reaching fixture git and meshd) | FAIL | Findings 1 and 2 |
| No assertion weakened, no fixture edited | PASS | `test_invariants.py` diff is additive only; `tests/fixtures/real/**` untouched |
| Commit author / one commit per sub-step | PASS | table above |
| Security, supervision, recovery | N/A | no daemon, authz, socket or supervisor code changed in this run |

## Findings

1. **MAJOR. `GitMeshHarness.get_env()` overwrites the harness env with the raw outer environment.**
   - Evidence: `tests/gitfixture.py:81` `env = dict(os.environ)` in `GitFixture.env()`, then `tests/gitfixture.py:208` `env.update(self.git_fixture.env())` in `GitMeshHarness.get_env()`. `MeshHarness.get_env()` (`tests/helpers.py:59–70`) first sets `PATH` to `[extra_path:]tests/shims:bin:$PATH`, `MESH_HOME`, `MESH_TESTING=1` and the per-harness `MESH_TRIPWIRE_FILE`. The update then puts back every key the outer env has: `PATH` loses the shims and `extra_path`, `MESH_TRIPWIRE_FILE` becomes the suite file, and an outer `MESH_HOME`/`MESH_TESTING` wins.
   - Consequences:
     - Outside `scripts/test.sh` (the plan tells coders to iterate with `python3 -m unittest …`), meshd and its children in every K/L test run without the tripwire shims on PATH. agy 1.5.3 is really installed on this box, so the A3 safety net is gone.
     - Under test.sh, the per-test `assert_tripwire_empty()` checks a file that nothing writes, so it is vacuous.
     - Tests that pass `extra_path` (the stub-dir pattern used across tests/integration) lose their stubs.
   - No test instantiates `GitMeshHarness`, so this went unnoticed.
   - Required change:
     - Add `GitFixture.git_env_vars()` returning only the hermetic keys (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, plus anything added under Finding 2).
     - Build `env()` from it, and have `GitMeshHarness.get_env()` do `env = super().get_env(); env.update(self.git_fixture.git_env_vars())`.
     - Add a daemon-free unit test: build `GitMeshHarness(fixture, extra_path=<a fixture dir>)` and assert that `PATH`, `MESH_HOME`, `MESH_TESTING` and `MESH_TRIPWIRE_FILE` equal `MeshHarness.get_env(h)`'s values and that the git keys are present. Then call `teardown()` with `check_invariants_on_teardown=False`, and assert both the harness home and the fixture base are gone.

2. **MAJOR. The fixture env is not hermetic against inherited `GIT_*` variables.**
   - Evidence: `tests/gitfixture.py:81–87` copies all of `os.environ` and only adds keys.
   - Any inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`/`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`, `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*` passes through to every fixture git call and, via `GitMeshHarness`, to meshd. `GIT_DIR` is set, for example, when the suite runs from a git hook or a wrapper.
   - With `GIT_DIR` set, git ignores the guarded `cwd` and operates on the repo `GIT_DIR` names. That is plan risk 2 (damage to the Mesh checkout), and the `/tmp/mh-` cwd guard does not stop it.
   - Inherited `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` reach meshd's env, which plan risk 6 forbids because it masks K8. The same leak would also break `test_k0_without_identity_requires_explicit_identity`.
   - The plan text says "`os.environ` plus …". Its stated intent (risks 2 and 6, "Never sets `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`") requires dropping them, so this is a conservative tightening, not a deviation.
   - Required change:
     - In the env builder, delete every key starting with `GIT_` from the copied environ before adding the hermetic keys.
     - Optionally set `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<base>` so discovery never walks above the fixture base.
     - Add a unit test: under `mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"GIT_DIR": <a second fixture-owned dir>, "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "leak", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "leak@example.invalid"})`, assert `env()` contains none of those keys and `make_k0(identity=False)` still refuses a commit without `-c` identity. Never point the patched `GIT_DIR` at the Mesh checkout.

3. **MAJOR. The I9 positive test does not use a merge commit, so I9's ancestor logic is untested on the case the plan names.**
   - Evidence:
     - `tests/unit/test_invariants.py:533` creates `mesh/prj_x/integration` at `main`'s initial commit in `setUp`.
     - `_merge_commit_on_integration` (`:625–635`) merges `mesh/prj_x/tsk_1` in `self.repo`, whose HEAD is `main`. That advances `main`, not the integration branch.
     - `:635` returns `head(self.repo, self.integration)`, which is still the initial commit.
   - The recorded `merge_commit` is therefore the integration tip itself. A wrong implementation that requires `merge_commit == integration tip` would pass all six I9 tests, and the docstring ("a real merge commit on the integration branch") is false.
   - Required change:
     - Make the merge on the integration branch, e.g. `worktree add <base>/integ mesh/prj_x/integration`, then `merge --no-ff --no-commit mesh/prj_x/tsk_1` and `commit` there with `identity=True`. Return that merge commit.
     - Assert it has a second parent (`rev-parse <sha>^2` rc 0) and differs from `main`'s initial commit.
     - Then add one more commit on the integration branch, so the recorded commit is a strict ancestor and not the tip, and expect `[]`.

4. **MINOR. `GitFixture.branches()` misparses branches checked out in linked worktrees.**
   - Evidence: `tests/gitfixture.py:164` strips only `"* "`. `git branch --list` marks branches checked out in another worktree with `+ ` (git ≥ 2.23; this box's git supports `init -b`, so it is ≥ 2.28). Task branches (`mesh/<prj>/<tsk>`) are exactly that case.
   - `branches()` would return `"+ mesh/…"`, so an `assertIn` fails and an `assertNotIn` (e.g. K12 "branch was not deleted / was deleted") can pass falsely.
   - Required change: use `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) refs/heads/<pattern>`, or `branch --list --format=%(refname:short) <pattern>`. Add a unit test with a branch checked out in a fixture worktree.

5. **MINOR. The guard checks only `cwd`, but the module docstring claims every path argument is checked.**
   - Evidence: `tests/gitfixture.py:8` ("every path argument is checked against that base before a process starts") versus `git()` (`:97–99`), which checks only `repo`.
   - `fixture.git(R, "-C", "/home/node/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1", "status")` passes the guard. So do `--git-dir=…`, `--work-tree=…` and absolute path arguments outside `/tmp/mh-`.
   - Required change: in `git()`, before spawning, reject the tokens `-C`, `--git-dir`/`--git-dir=*` and `--work-tree`/`--work-tree=*`, and any argument that starts with `/` and is not under `/tmp/mh-`. Add the `-C <mesh checkout>` case to `test_guard_refuses_paths_outside_base_before_spawn`. Alternatively, correct the docstring, but the check is preferred.

6. **MINOR. The fixture test module carries an `ACC: A8` tag.**
   - Evidence: `tests/unit/test_gitfixture.py:3` `ACC: A8 (supporting fixture for K1-K14; no ACC tag of its own)`. The plan says the fixture has no ACC tag. The tag makes `grep -rn "ACC: A8" tests` list tests that never check invariants.
   - Required change: remove the `ACC: A8` token and keep the text "supporting fixture for K1–K14 (fixture K0)".

7. **MINOR. I9 violation reasons do not separate git errors from real negatives.**
   - Evidence: `mesh/core/invariants.py:567` treats any non-zero `merge-base --is-ancestor` result as "not an ancestor", but rc 1 means "not an ancestor" while rc 128 means an error (unknown integration branch, not a git repo). Likewise `:555` reports "does not exist in the repo" when `repo_path` is not a git repo at all.
   - The `merge_commit` value goes into argv unvalidated. Today a value starting with `-` only produces a wrong reason, but the reason is misleading.
   - Recommended change (behaviour stays "one I9 violation"):
     - rc 1 → "not an ancestor"; any other rc → `"git merge-base failed (rc N): <stderr tail>"`.
     - Check `merge_commit` against `^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$` first (reason "merge_commit is not a sha").
     - Pass `refs/heads/<integration_branch>` to avoid a tag/branch name clash.

## Notes for Quest (no coder action)

- **Where this file lives.** This file was written in the r1 worktree because the profile refused the write in `/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1` and `/home/node/workspace/mesh-fresh-v1`. Copy it to main's `docs/coordination/reviews/m2-r1.md`. It is untracked in `wt/m2-r1`, so the coder must not commit it.
- **Scope string.** The review request's range `6e4871f..HEAD` resolves on main to coordination-only commits. Use `6e4871f..wt/m2-r1` (or the worktree) in the next review request.
- **Guard vs. r4+ tests.** `git()` requires `cwd` under the fixture base, but code-task worktrees live under the harness home (`$H/workspaces/…`, a different `/tmp/mh-*` dir). The common block says test commits in task worktrees go "via the fixture helper", which this guard refuses. Before r3/r4, decide one of two options and put it in those prompts:
  - (a) K tests set `workspaces.root` to a dir under the fixture base (mode 0700);
  - (b) `GitMeshHarness` registers its own home as a second allowed root (it must start with `/tmp/mh-`).
  I recommend (b): it keeps `workspaces.root` at its default and is a few lines in gitfixture.py.
- **A1 margin.** 588 s under concurrent worktree load leaves 12 s of headroom, before M1c runs 2b–5 and M2 add tests. Plan Q1 applies: re-time on a quiet host at the M1c gate.
